title: Small Business Flexibility Act
committees: H-Education and Workforce Committee: Referred To 2025-01-03
latest_action: Referred to the House Committee on Education and Workforce.
summary: Small Business Flexibility Act This bill provides statutory authority for the pooling of tips among two pools of employees. The first pool consists of employees who customarily and regularly receive tips (as is permitted under the current statute). The second pool consists of (1) employees who customarily and regularly receive tips and are paid at least minimum wage, and (2) employees who do not customarily and regularly receive tips.

income.magnitude_note: Moves tip income among restaurant workers; no federal budget effect.
income.justification: Tip pooling with back-of-house staff shifts money from servers to cooks and dishwashers, both low-wage groups, so the score stays near the middle. Employers gain flexibility that can lower what they must pay untipped staff, which nudges the score slightly positive.
income.rater: claude-fable-5-1 (chat session; rubric v1.1 applied by hand - preview, not a scorer run)

households_business.justification: Tipped workers could see their tips shared more widely; untipped coworkers could gain. Restaurant owners gain control over how tips are distributed.
households_business.rater: claude-fable-5-1 (chat session; rubric v1.1 applied by hand - preview, not a scorer run)

plain.one_sentence: Lets employers pool tips between servers and kitchen or other staff who don't normally get tips, as long as everyone in the pool is paid at least minimum wage.
plain.status_plain: Still just a proposal - most bills never get a vote

if_you_are.worker: If you earn tips, more of them could be shared with coworkers; if you work in the kitchen, you could receive a share.
if_you_are.small_business_owner: You could set up a tip pool that includes back-of-house staff.

plain.what_it_does_not_do: It does not let owners or managers keep tips.
